analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow excerpts and changed-range context. In .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml head lines 63–75, 181–193 and 311–323, new cache admission skips Actions cache steps on darkbloom-* runners lacking DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL; visible restore/save conditions enforce that choice. Head lines 106–131, 218–243 and 348–373 strengthen restored .git checks before ordinary Git operations by rejecting symlinks, nonsample hooks, fsmonitor/hooksPath configuration and includes, while retaining connectivity validation. These are hardening changes, not supported regressions; the checks do not establish authenticity of cache contents.
Reviewed base lines 519–1067 and 1068–1230 for coverage artifacts, blocking versus nonblocking cluster checks, release-build cache reuse, focused checks and the final selected-lane gate. The range map places additional cache changes in later head sections not supplied here; no unrelated gate weakening is established. Workflow permissions remain contents:read and visible checkouts disable credential persistence. No changed handling of prompts, encryption, serving authorization, billing or privileged helpers is shown (A-001/A-003, T-008/T-041, T-052–T-054, T-044–T-062).
Integration must verify the new cache-admission contract across provider-ci-build and other changed cache users: setting DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL is only tested for presence here, not used to configure the pinned cache action. Runner-side endpoint selection, isolation and credential handling are outside this evidence, not observed missing controls. Review those changes and the later workflow head sections before concluding that adversarial provider-operated runners cannot access or contaminate trusted build caches (A-017/T-054). No cache URL secrecy or external cache implementation is assumed.
